properties.decision:
UNDECIDED, recorded 2026-07-28. schema/structure.yaml:108 declares an Anchor node type with design_intent, key_decisions, checksum and created_at. Nothing in the core creates it, nothing reads it, there is no node::ANCHOR constant, and reflow2's own design contains ZERO instances. It was superseded: temporal.rs:62 describes Snapshot as "a checksummed baseline (generalizes the P2 to P3 Anchor)", and Snapshot has 14 live instances while DriftEvent has 37.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN TIDYING: the schema still advertises the type, and does so from BOTH SIDES of a relationship that cannot exist.

(1) describe_schema returns Anchor to any agent asking what the vocabulary contains, serving this hint with it — "A checksummed baseline of the design taken when leaving P2 for a build round (P3). Not extracted from prose — created by the workflow at the structure to build transition. DriftEvents reference the Anchor they diverged from."

(2) AMENDED 2026-07-28, reviewing resync_protocol.json and phase_transitions.json: DriftEvent's OWN extraction_hint (schema/verify.yaml:63) makes the matching claim from the other end — "A recorded divergence between the design (graph/Anchor) and reality (filesystem/build). Produced by drift detection, not extracted from prose. References the Anchor it diverged from via DEPENDS_ON." No DriftEvent references an Anchor, because none exists; all 37 reference something else. So the vocabulary describes a DEPENDS_ON relationship between two types in both directions, and that relationship has zero instances and no code path that could create one. An agent reading either hint and following it creates a node nothing will ever read, and believes it has anchored a build round.

Three options. (a) RETIRE the type from the schema, which is the honest reading if Snapshot fully covers it — but removing a node type strands any graph that already carries one, the same objection that kept `review` and `simulation` in Verification.method when the taxonomy grew. (b) IMPLEMENT it, if the P2-to-P3 anchoring semantics are meant to survive as something distinct from a general Snapshot. (c) REDIRECT — keep the name as an alias or documented synonym of Snapshot so old graphs still load, while the discovery surface stops advertising it as a separate thing to create.

Whichever is chosen, TWO hints must move with it, not one — that is what the amendment adds. And the question underneath is the same one dec:one-retire-edge asks about edges: what should CONSULT the retirement, and does a retired vocabulary item stop being offered or get offered with a warning?
properties.name: OPEN — the Anchor node type is superseded by Snapshot but still advertised: retire it or implement it?
properties.rationale: Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow's workflow_master.json, whose architecture_anchor is the mechanism this type was modelled on. Recorded rather than fixed because all three options are defensible and the choice is Anthony's — it is a vocabulary call, and those have been his every time. Note the shape it shares with the other findings from this review: a schema declaring something no computation reaches (req:functional-vocabulary-computes), a default asserting a choice nobody made (req:defaults-do-not-assert, req:edge-defaults-do-not-assert), and now a whole TYPE advertised on the discovery surface after being superseded. This is the same defect at node-type granularity, which is the level the earlier sweeps did not examine — they measured properties, not types.
